version.changelog: 改回中文名称，移除PROXY_TOKEN硬编码

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed Chinese-language visa guide with a bounded local script, but users should verify live policy results because it may pull general Google snippets rather than official-only sources.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares PROXY_TOKEN and describes a proxy/API data flow, but the inspected script does not read environment variables and only performs a Google search for the policy-update path.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, dependency installation, remote code retrieval, or package-manager behavior was found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to invoking the bundled Python script with JSON parameters, and the Chinese-citizen/Chinese-language scope is explicit in the artifact, though the frontmatter tool name is broader than the internal subcommands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No file writes, persistence mechanisms, privilege escalation, background workers, credential-store access, or destructive behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose, static visa database, checklist generation, and policy-update lookup are coherent for a China-focused visa guidance skill; the main quality risk is that live policy updates can include unverified web-search snippets.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a Chinese-language visa helper that may send destination-based policy queries to Google for latest updates. Use it for planning checklists, but verify visa requirements and recent changes against official embassy, consulate, or immigration websites before booking or traveling.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network-backed lookup is disclosed in the data-flow section, but the artifact does not tightly document allowed external destinations beyond saying policy updates use online search.
[SQP-3] expected: The China-specific, Chinese-language scope is explicit in the name, description, script docstring, and user-facing examples.
[SQP-2] expected: The policy-update feature intentionally performs an external search using only the destination and visa-policy query terms; it would be clearer if Google were named before use.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Generic Google result snippets are not an authoritative source for visa-policy guidance, so users should treat live update output as a lead to verify, not as final advice.
[SDI-1] expected: The broader web-search trust boundary is disclosed at a high level and does not show credential use or exfiltration, but official-source restriction would reduce misinformation risk.
